question: Which NFA variant retained the most capacity after 100 cycles at C/3, what are its aluminium and iron contents, and what c lattice parameter does Table 1 give for it?

trace.query: SELECT id, page, text FROM atoms WHERE text ILIKE '%retention%' OR text ILIKE '%100 cycles%' OR text ILIKE '%C/3%' OR text ILIKE '%cycle%' ORDER BY page, id LIMIT 80
SELECT * FROM cells WHERE table_id='p5.T1' ORDER BY row_no, col_no
SELECT id, page, text FROM lines WHERE page IN (4,5,10,11) AND (text ILIKE '%NFA%' OR text ILIKE '%Al%' OR text ILIKE '%retention%' OR text ILIKE '%C/3%') ORDER BY page, line_no
SELECT id, page, text FROM atoms WHERE text ILIKE '%rich%' OR text ILIKE '%NFA-A%' OR text ILIKE '%NFA-F%' ORDER BY page, id
SELECT id, page, text FROM lines WHERE page=11 AND line_no BETWEEN 52 AND 60 OR page=10 AND line_no BETWEEN 30 AND 36 OR page=5 AND line_no BETWEEN 83 AND 90 ORDER BY page, line_no
SELECT regexp_extract(text, 'Fe([0-9.]+)Al[0-9.]+O2 \(NFA-A\)', 1) AS fe_content, regexp_extract(text, 'Fe[0-9.]+Al([0-9.]+)O2 \(NFA-A\)', 1) AS al_content FROM lines WHERE id='p11.L54'

rendered:
The variant that retained the most capacity is NFA-A, the Al-rich variant, at ≈80% capacity retention after 100 cycles at C/3[1] (the other variants fall lower; see Fig. 8[2]).
Its composition is printed as LiNi0.8Fe0.05Al0.15O2[3].
Iron content (Fe, per formula unit): 0.05[4].
Aluminium content (Al, per formula unit): 0.15[5].
The c lattice parameter in Table 1[6] for the row labelled Al-rich NFA[7] is 14.2232(4)[8]. The table does not print the name NFA-A itself; this row is matched to NFA-A by its Al-rich label (the Fe-rich row corresponds to NFA-F).
